A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we derive theoretical bounds to predict the long-term influence and the emergence of a giant connected component, and that we show empirically that the bounds are tight.

The main takeaway from our work is that
, in the sub-critical region, a node's influence is bounded by a function of its degree and the spectral radius of the network, which is independent of the network size.
, in a diffusion model, the influence of an initial seed set is bounded by the spectral radius of the adjacency matrix of the network.
